title: Canonical representable slice density in a space-valued presheaf infinity category
statement:
Use the universes, quasicategories, coherent functors, full subcategories, equivalences and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the space categories of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$. Let $D$ be a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory, put $\mathcal P(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$, and let $y:D\to\mathcal P(D)$ be $d\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_D(-,d)$. Let $A$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal P(D)$ on the objects equivalent to some $y(d)$. For each $F\in\mathcal P(D)$ define
$$A_{/F}:=A\times_{\mathcal P(D)}\mathcal P(D)_{/F},$$
where an $n$-simplex of $\mathcal P(D)_{/F}$ is a map $\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathcal P(D)$ whose final vertex is $F$, and the projection restricts it to its initial face. Thus a vertex of $A_{/F}$ is an arrow $a\to F$ with $a\in A$. Appending $F$ gives the canonical cocone $\delta_F:(A_{/F})^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal P(D)$ on the source projection, with apex $F$. The quasicategory $A_{/F}$ is essentially $\mathcal U$-small, meaning equivalent to a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory. The cocone $\delta_F$ is colimiting. These assertions hold for the canonical cocone, including all its higher simplices, rather than merely for some presentation of $F$ as a colimit of representables.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.3 and its proof, printed pp. 325-326 (PDF pp. 343-344); Lemma 5.1.5.5 proof, printed pp. 326-327, for the small representable slice. Replete-image formulation uses essential smallness instead of literal smallness. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.

proof.text: Keep $\mathcal U$ fixed and work in a larger universe $\mathcal W$ containing $\mathcal P(D)$, its slices and their functor categories. This changes neither $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ nor the desired smallness assertion. By [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], each presheaf $F$ has a $\mathcal U$-small right-fibration representative $q:E_F\to D$. Its total space is a quasicategory: project an inner horn to $D$, fill there and lift by the right-fibration horn condition. For two such representatives the same statement identifies the presheaf mapping space with the Kan complex $\operatorname{Fun}_{/D}(E_F,E_G)$. This complex is $\mathcal U$-small degree by degree, since $D,E_F,E_G$ are small. Thus $\mathcal P(D)$ is locally $\mathcal U$-small. By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] the actual Yoneda functor $y$ is fully faithful. Its factorization $J:D\to A$ is fully faithful as well, since $A$ is full. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to obtain a coherent equivalence $J:D\simeq A$. Both categories fit in $\mathcal W$; that statement does not require $A$ to be $\mathcal U$-small.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.3, first two sentences; Proposition 5.1.3.1; Sections 2.2.1 and 3.3.2 for the existing transport model.

proof.text: Put $T=A_{/F}$ and $B=D\times_{\mathcal P(D)}\mathcal P(D)_{/F}=D\times_A T$. The slice projection is a right fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]; its pullbacks are right fibrations because a lifting problem in a pullback is precisely a lifting problem over the specified simplex of the base. They are quasicategories by the inner-horn argument of step 1. The join-slice and pullback clauses of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] identify $B\to D$ as the right fibration classified by $d\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(y(d),F)$. The natural equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation] identifies this classifier with $F$. The mapping-space and composition clauses of transport therefore give over-maps $s:E_F\to B$ and $t:B\to E_F$ representing inverse equivalences, with homotopies $ts\simeq1$ and $st\simeq1$ in their Kan over-map spaces. Evaluating such homotopies gives coherent transformations of total categories whose components lie in the Kan vertex fibers; their edges have inverses there. By the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] these are natural equivalences. Hence $s$ is an equivalence of quasicategories over $D$. Compose $s$ with $B\to T$ and append $F$ to obtain a join cocone $\alpha$ on $yq$. Under the arrow-to-join comparison in the transport statement, the coherent cocone has leg at $e\in E_F$ corresponding to the element of $F(q(e))$ represented by $e$, by the specified Yoneda evaluation. This construction and identification take place in the spaces of over-maps, including their parameter simplices; they do not choose unrelated individual legs.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.2 and its right-fibration interpretation; canonical cocone of Lemma 5.1.5.3.

proof.text: The projection $v:B\to T$ is an equivalence, as follows directly from the right-fibration morphism formula [lem-cbc-right-fibration-morphism-space]. For $b,b'\in B$ over $d,d'$, that formula expresses $\operatorname{Map}_B(b,b')$ as the homotopy fiber at $b$ of the transport map $\operatorname{Map}_D(d,d')\to B_d$. The analogous formula in $T$ uses $\operatorname{Map}_A(Jd,Jd')\to T_{Jd}$. Here $B_d=T_{Jd}$ degree by degree, and $J$ induces an equivalence of the mapping spaces. Choose the transport in B by pulling back that in T, as allowed by the stated pullback compatibility of the morphism formula; this makes the square of transport maps commute. Then [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] identify their homotopy fibers, proving that $v$ is fully faithful. To check essential surjectivity, let $u\in T$ lie over $a\in A$ and choose an equivalence $h:Jd\to a$. The $n=1$ right-horn lifting condition gives an edge $\widetilde h:u'\to u$ over $h$, where $u'$ is in the image of $B$. This edge is an equivalence by the following two-horn argument. For any edge $f:x\to y$ in a right fibration lying over an equivalence $h$, take the base inverse triangle with edges $h^{-1},h,1$. The right horn $\Lambda^2_2$ with edges $12=f$ and $02=1_y$ lifts this triangle and supplies $g:y\to x$ with $[f][g]=1_y$. Repeat with $g$ to obtain $k:x\to y$ and $[g][k]=1_x$. The composition laws of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] give $[f]=[f][g][k]=[k]$, hence $[g][f]=1_x$. That node's equivalence criterion now makes $f$ an equivalence. Thus the full essential image of $v$ is all of $T$, and [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] supplies a coherent quasi-inverse. Consequently $e=vs:E_F\simeq T$ proves essential $\mathcal U$-smallness. The restriction of the actual canonical cocone $\delta_F$ along $e$ is the join cocone $\alpha$ of step 2, with its entire simplicial boundary.

source.place: Replete-image expansion of Lemma 5.1.5.3; direct right-fibration proof of equivalence on slices.

proof.text:
Here is the sections calculation needed to prove that this particular $\alpha$ is colimiting. Let $K$ be a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory and let a small right fibration $Q\to K$ classify $H:K^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$. Put $\Gamma=\operatorname{Fun}_{/K}(K,Q)$. Transport classification [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], applied to the constant one-point functor, says that $\Gamma$ is a small Kan space. For every small Kan complex $X$, the constant-product clause and the degreewise exponential adjunction give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(X,\Gamma)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(X,\Gamma)\cong\operatorname{Fun}_{/K}(K\times X,Q)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)}(\Delta X,H).$$
The first comparison is the enriched mapping-space comparison of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], applied to the simplicial category of small Kan complexes. The middle map sends $f$ to $(k,x)\mapsto f(x)(k)$ on every parameter simplex; the last is precisely transport for the constant classifier $K\times X$. Thus this composite is induced by the evaluation cone $\Delta\Gamma\to H$. The cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] shows that the evaluation cone is limiting: $\Gamma\simeq\lim_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}H$. This calculation is natural under pullback and postcomposition, because all three displayed comparisons are.

source.place: Contravariant form of Corollary 3.3.3.4, derived explicitly from transport and the exponential adjunction.

proof.text:
For a test presheaf $G$, choose its small classifier $E_G\to D$. An over-map $E_F\to E_G$ is exactly a section of $E_F\times_D E_G\to E_F$; the correspondence sends $f$ to $e\mapsto(e,f(e))$ and is an isomorphism in every simplicial degree, also with every parameter $\Delta^n$. By [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] this pullback classifies $Gq^{\mathrm{op}}$. Step 4 yields
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(F,G)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{/E_F}(E_F,E_F\times_DE_G)\simeq\lim_{e\in E_F^{\mathrm{op}}}G(q(e))\simeq\lim_{e\in E_F^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(y(q(e)),G).$$
The last equivalence is the coherent natural Yoneda evaluation of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation]. This is the actual comparison induced by $\alpha$: an over-map representing $g:F\to G$ sends $e=(d,x)$ to $g_d(x)$; evaluation at $1_d$ of the composite $y(d)\xrightarrow{\alpha_e}F\xrightarrow{g}G$ is the same $g_d(x)$. The composition and unit comparisons in transport and the naturality of Yoneda evaluation make this calculation commute with the entire parameter simplex and all operators. Therefore it identifies the full comparison maps, not merely their action on vertices. The colimit mapping-space criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] proves that $\alpha$ is colimiting.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.3; mapping-space verification of its canonical cocone using right-fibration sections.

proof.text: For completeness, transport from the small index to the full replete slice uses only coherent functor equivalences. Choose a coherent quasi-inverse $r:T\to E_F$ to $e$ from step 3. Precomposition $e^*:\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathcal P(D))\to\operatorname{Fun}(E_F,\mathcal P(D))$ and $r^*$ have inverse natural equivalences obtained by whiskering the unit and counit of $e,r$. The componentwise criterion and mapping-space invariance in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore show that restriction induces an equivalence on the spaces of coherent cocones from the source diagram to each constant $G$. It fixes $G$ and sends $\delta_F$ to $\alpha$, since this is precomposition of the actual appended-vertex simplicial map. In the square whose upper map is composition with $\delta_F$, whose lower map is composition with $\alpha$, whose left side is the identity on $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(F,G)$ and whose right side is this restriction equivalence, the lower map is an equivalence by step 5. Hence the upper map is an equivalence. The dual cone criterion in the same node proves that $\delta_F$ itself is colimiting. Apply that criterion in the enlarged ambient universe containing $T$; only the equivalence $T\simeq E_F$ uses $\mathcal U$-smallness. This proves both requested assertions for the specified canonical cocone and all its higher simplices.
